name_note: GTDB uses the current name Anaerobutyricum hallii; most published work calls the species Eubacterium hallii.

sentences.text: A strain related to Eubacterium hallii and isolated from infant faeces was separated as a new species when the genus Anaerobutyricum was created.
The species uses glucose and the fermentation intermediates acetate and lactate to form butyrate and hydrogen, and converts 1,2-propanediol to propionate.
A cohort study identified it as one of the first butyrate producers in the infant gut; faecal libraries from four countries were screened for it.
It cannot break down complex oligosaccharides or polysaccharides itself, but grows on fermentation metabolites released by other gut bacteria.
Oral treatment of obese diabetic mice with the live bacterium improved insulin sensitivity and increased energy expenditure.
